question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹4,000 at 6.75% per annum rate of interest deposited on 24 February 2024 and withdrawn on 25 April 2024.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total days: **February** (5 days) + **March** (31 days) + **April** (25 days) = **61 days**.

As **2024** is a **leap year**, total days = **366**.

Time (T) = 61 ÷ 366 = **1/6 years**.

Simple Interest = (4000 × 6.75 × 1) ÷ (100 × 6) = 40 × 1.125 = **₹45**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹45.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹4,000

**Rate (R)** = 6.75% per annum

**Time Period:** 24 February 2024 to 25 April 2024

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8925ee7cbe5f256d9cec138b4fc408fb83f0be706dbb755c37680b39c8c98605.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ **Leap Year Check:** 2024 is divisible by 4, so it has **366 days**.

⇒ **Days in Feb:** 29 − 24 = **5 days**.

⇒ **Days in Mar:** **31 days**.

⇒ **Days in Apr:** **25 days**.

⇒ **Total Days:** 5 + 31 + 25 = **61 days**.

⇒ **Simple Interest (SI) formula:** SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (4000 × 6.75 × (61 ÷ 366)) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (4000 × 6.75 × 1 ÷ 6) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (40 × 6.75) ÷ 6

⇒ SI = 270 ÷ 6

⇒ SI = **₹45**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹45.**

**__Additional Information__**

Leap Year Calculation

A **leap year** occurs every 4 years and contains **366 days** (February has 29 days). For calculating interest, the denominator changes from 365 to 366.

Counting Days for Interest

In banking practice, the **day of deposit** is usually excluded and the **day of withdrawal** is included when calculating the interest period.

Simple Interest Formula

**SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100**, where P is Principal, R is Rate per annum, and T is Time in years.
